There is no distinct top plane, no clear front-edge line and no eave shadow. Below that strip is a front face with the blue plaque (rows 57-60) and a light row 61. A dark outline closes the block at row 62. The pedestal therefore reads as a front elevation with at most a rim. The post (rows 34-53) is a thin vertical shaft. The lantern is drawn as a vertical glass face (rows 23-28) with a small gold crown (rows 17-20) and a blue band at row 21 over a dark row 22. That is a weak roof hint, not an ellipse, and the crown is a small detail on the lantern. The pedestal is the large part with no real top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The lamp is tiny and thin on the board. The pedestal reads as a pale grey block with a small plaque and only about 2-3 value steps, with no stone-by-stone shading or grain. The iron post is a near-flat dark line. The lantern is a small yellow and dark cluster, and the described gold bands, curled brackets, octagonal glass facets and crown cap are barely visible. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted rather than sticker-black, which counts in its favour. The visible-tone count of 4 per tile is far below the richer references (well 20, stall 17, hedge 9). The sparse crook lamp has a tone count of 0, so that fact is not held against the candidate. By eye, though, the royal lamp is meant to be an ornate piece and looks flatter and thinner than the Beodeul props, closer to a simple sticker-like silhouette. When in doubt, fail.
